name: AL-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 33 points, among the reddest House seats
Incumbent Aderholt holds a massive cash advantage ($750k vs $396)
Challenger raised only about $16k with no outside spending on either side
Markets price a Republican win at 99%; no polls or expert ratings track the race
model.rationale: A 33-point Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with under $500 in the bank leave no visible Democratic path; fundamentals and prediction markets both point to a lopsided Republican win.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal or a historic national wave could put this district in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 4th district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 33 points to the right. Republican incumbent Robert Aderholt is seeking re-election and reported about $1.02 million raised with $750,000 on hand. Democratic nominee Amanda Pusczek has raised about $15,600 and had under $500 in the bank, with no outside spending reported on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets put the Republican's chance of winning at about 99%. With the district's deep red lean and that lopsided financial picture, the seat sits firmly in the Republican column. The main uncertainty comes from the absence of polling, but nothing in the available evidence suggests the race is close.
